newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK pays last pre-handover visit to leader's house.
newsitem.headline: HK pays last pre-handover visit to leader's house.

text.p: Thousands of people visited the grounds of the Hong Kong Governor's house on Sunday to savour the springtime floral splendour of its gardens for the last time before the end of British rule in the territory.

The Government House shook off its usual aloofness and opened its gates to visitors over the weekend for its last annual open day ahead of the territory's return to China on July 1, after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
"I must take pictures because it's a last visit," said one visitor who had queued for hours before seeing the home of Hong Kong's colonial rulers.
About 66,400 people had visited the Government House since Saturday by 2.00 p.m. local time (0600 GMT), a government spokeswoman said.
Reuters estimated a total of 90,000 weekend visitors by the end of Sunday.
Last year, the garden played host to some 24,000 visitors on a single open day.

The fate of the Government House and its open-day tradition after the handover remain uncertain. Chief executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa, who will take over from Governor Chris Patten, has not decided whether to move into the building.
